name: Ater
overview: Ater is a male biblical figure known primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. The Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details beyond this significant familial connection. His mention highlights the restoration of the Jewish community following exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Ater appears as a proper name in Scripture and may mean 'crippled one,' 'left-handed one,' or 'Etir.' These possible meanings reflect the Hebrew roots of the name but do not indicate that the name was given directly by God. The name is recorded in Ezra 2:15.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ater as a descendant of Hezekiah, suggesting a royal or notable lineage. Beyond this inferred relationship and the mention of his sons who returned from captivity, no further family details are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ater's significance lies in his role as an ancestor whose descendants participated in the post-exilic restoration of Judah, marking a continuation of God's covenant people after a period of judgment and exile. This connection to Hezekiah situates Ater within the broader narrative of God's faithfulness to His promises through the preservation of Davidic lineage and the reestablishment of the community in the land.
